title: Fisherman's rib lap throw
subtitle: A springy 100 by 120 cm lap throw in fisherman's rib on 5 mm needles.
excerpt: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw worked flat in fisherman's rib on 5 mm needles. Fisherman's rib produces a deeper, springier fabric than standard 1×1 rib by knitting into the stitch below. About 850 g of DK on larger needles, or 500 g of aran.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 11th series (1895), §Fisherman's Rib, describes the knit-below technique for a thick rib fabric suitable for scarves and knee rugs. Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Fisherman's Rib, confirms the k1b method and notes the doubled-thickness quality for warmth.

knitting.gaugeText: 16 sts × 30 rows = 10 × 10 cm in fisherman's rib on 5 mm needles, unblocked. The rib draws in by roughly 30%; the throw knits wider than it looks on the needles.

glossaryTerms.definition: A rib stitch worked by knitting into the stitch in the row below (k1b) instead of the current stitch, combined with slipping the stitch above it. The result is a deep, springy rib fabric that looks similar to brioche but is worked with a different method. Fisherman's rib lies flat and is reversible.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 5 mm needles in
fisherman's rib
, finishing at 100 cm wide by 120 cm long.

Single-panel construction; no seaming. Fisherman's rib was chosen because it produces a deeper, springier fabric than standard 1×1 rib from the same yarn weight and needle: the knit-below technique creates a doubled column that adds warmth without adding bulk. At DK on 5 mm needles, the finished throw is as warm as a standard aran-weight project. Budget about 850 g (about 1,870 m / 2,045 yards) of DK. Buy in matched dye lots. The throw will relax in width off the needles; measure after the first wash and flat dry to confirm finished dimensions.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 850 g (about 1,870 m / 2,045 yards) of DK-weight yarn. A smooth merino or merino blend DK shows the rib cleanly.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 5 mm (UK 6 / US 8) circular needle, 120 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

16 stitches and 30 rows to 10 cm in fisherman's rib on 5 mm needles, lightly stretched after washing. Fisherman's rib draws in significantly on the needle; measure the swatch after a wash and gentle flat stretch to the natural relaxed width rather than measuring it tightly clamped.
If your stitch gauge is 14 per 10 cm with 160 stitches, the throw will be about 114 cm wide in the relaxed state. Adjust the cast-on in multiples of 2 to hit your target width.
Stitches used

items.name: k1b
items.qty: knit into the stitch in the row below the next stitch on the left needle, then slip the stitch above off the needle

content.text: Pattern
Cast-on
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 160 stitches (a multiple of 2). Long-tail tail: (5 × 160) / 10 + 15 = 80 + 15 = 95 cm. Measure 110 cm of tail.
Setup row
Row 1 (WS setup): *k1, p1; repeat from * to end. This plain rib row creates the first row of loops that k1b will knit into.
Body
All subsequent rows: *k1b, p1; repeat from * to end.

The same row is repeated on every pass. The knit-below stitch will draw from the row below on each pass, creating the deep rib automatically. When you set this aside between sessions, every row is the same: k1b, p1 to end.
Stitch count check-ins
At row 180 (about 60 cm): count across. You should have 160 stitches. Fisherman's rib never changes stitch count. At row 358 (about 119 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults

Knitting the current row's stitch rather than the one below: the stitch below is the prominent elongated loop hanging below the stitch on the left needle. Insert the needle into that loop, not the loop on the needle itself.

Stitch count rising: the slipped stitch above the k1b was not slipped, both the below loop and the current stitch were knitted. This adds an extra stitch. Check that the old stitch slides cleanly off the left needle after each k1b.
Cast-off
Cast off in rib pattern (k1b, p1 alternating) with needles one size larger than the throw needles. Fisherman's rib is highly elastic and a tight cast-off will compress the edge noticeably.
Finishing
Weave in both ends along the rib columns. Lay flat for a minute after washing to confirm the width has relaxed to the finished measurement before drying in position.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. Lay flat to dry, spreading to the relaxed width. Fisherman's rib does not need blocking to lie flat.
What to try next

From fisherman's rib, try brioche rib next. The two techniques produce nearly the same fabric. Brioche uses slip stitches and yarn-overs instead of knit-below. Brioche also scales easily to two-colour work.
